title: Load one measurement library per page
statement: Each measurement product is loaded once per document, with no second copy arriving from a tag manager, a framework integration, or a template that also injects it.
rationale: A second copy of the same library counts every event twice, so the numbers used to judge whether any other change worked are wrong before the change is made.
implementation: Choose one installation route per product and remove the others, rather than adding a guard that tolerates duplicate loads. Check the tag manager container as well as the application source.

verification.method: Load representative routes in a browser and count requests for each measurement library and the global objects it installs.

caution: Removing an installation route stops data flowing through it, which breaks any report built on that route, so the redundant copy is identified for review rather than deleted outright.

title: Preserve the referrer across internal redirects
statement: A request that passes through the site's own redirects arrives at the destination still carrying the referrer the original request had, and the site's referrer policy does not strip it on same-origin hops.
rationale: A redirect that discards the referrer turns identifiable arrivals into unattributed ones, so traffic the site did earn appears to have come from nowhere.
implementation: Set the referrer policy deliberately rather than inheriting a default from a framework template or an edge configuration, and reduce redirect hops so fewer opportunities to lose the value exist.

verification.method: Follow representative internal redirect chains with a referrer set and record the value present at each hop and at the destination.

caution: The specification defines how policies control the referrer without stating which policy a site should choose, and a stricter policy may be a deliberate privacy decision that outranks attribution. Divergence is reported with that possibility named.

title: State the limits of assistant referral attribution
statement: Reports naming traffic from an AI assistant say how the classification was made and what it cannot see, and never present a share of unattributed traffic as though its origin were known.
rationale: Assistant referrals arrive with incomplete or absent origin information, so a confident figure for them is produced by assumption rather than by measurement and then gets treated as evidence.
implementation: Record the matching rule used for each classified source alongside the figure, and report unclassified arrivals as unclassified rather than distributing them across known sources.

verification.method: Review each report that attributes traffic to an assistant and confirm it names its classification rule and its unattributed residual.

caution: This constrains how this process reports, not how a site behaves, so it asserts nothing about any platform and needs no citation. No arrival count here supports a claim about whether an assistant cited the site.

title: Exclude personal data from addresses and measurement payloads
statement: No address that reaches a measurement endpoint carries an email, a name, an account identifier, or a token, whether in a path segment, a query parameter, or a fragment forwarded by script.
rationale: An address sent to measurement is stored by the receiving service and appears in reports many people can read, so a personal detail placed there is disclosed well beyond the request that carried it.
implementation: Carry identifiers in the request body or the session rather than the address, and strip known personal parameters before the measurement call rather than after it has been sent.

verification.method: Capture outbound measurement requests across authenticated and unauthenticated routes and scan the transmitted addresses and payloads for personal-data patterns.

caution: Detection here is pattern-based and finds the shapes it recognises, so a clean result means no known pattern matched rather than no personal data present.

title: Record one pageview per navigation in a client-routed app
statement: A client-side route change emits exactly one pageview, the initial document load emits exactly one, and a restoration from the back-forward cache emits one or none according to a stated choice rather than by accident.
rationale: Manual instrumentation added alongside a library that already tracks history changes double-counts every navigation, and a restored page that silently re-fires inflates the count for whichever pages readers navigate back to most.
implementation: Disable the library's automatic history tracking or the application's manual call, never both at once, and decide explicitly what a restored navigation should emit.

verification.method: Drive a browser through initial load, several client-side navigations, and a back-forward restoration, counting pageview events emitted at each step.

sources.title: HTML Standard: navigation and session history APIs

title: Report measurement against the canonical address
statement: The page identity sent to measurement is the canonical address the page declares, so tracking parameters, alternate casing, and trailing-slash variants collapse onto one row instead of several.
rationale: A page split across rows by parameter variants looks like several low-traffic pages, which hides both its real total and any change to it.
implementation: Read the canonical value the document already emits and send that as the page identity, rather than sending the current address and normalising it later in the reporting layer.

verification.method: Request pages through parameterised and alternate-form addresses and compare the page identity transmitted against the canonical value each response declares.

caution: That one page should occupy one row is a consistency property of the site's own reporting rather than a platform behaviour, so no citation applies. Where a parameter genuinely changes the content, the variants are distinct pages and collapsing them would be the error.
